steps.content: Teeth gritted, you pull from your last dregs of energy. A faint, shimmering barrier of shackles barely materializes, deflecting her sudden lunge.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: I saw that last night. What is it? Outland sorcery? Are you with Fraser? Eastia?
You call it Outland. So you really are from DisCity. That means we're not enemies.
Your barrier shatters upon her strike before you can finish speaking. The impact sends you staggering back, your spine cracking against the damp stone wall.
Cough... What's the matter? My DisCity accent not up to your standards?

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: Why are you here?
I told you. I was separated from my companions, swept here by the Black Tide.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: I mean now!
I came upstairs looking for help. I need to get back to DisCity. To my people.
You barely sidestep a lethal strike. Her attacks come faster now, a relentless flurry that tears open old wounds as the Black Ring's pressure turns your limbs to lead.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: They can't come here. No one can get close!
I made it here, didn't I? How do you know it's impossible if you don't try?

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: That was just your damn bad luck!
She closes the distance, grabbing your shoulders and slamming you back against the cold railing. When the blade rises for a final thrust—
You rip away the blood-soaked bandage, shoving the raw wound toward her face. The metallic scent explodes between you; she reels back as if scalded.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: ...You... cheap shot!
But it worked.
The sound of her ragged, trembling breath is your cue. You shove her back, creating a precious few feet of space.
Why are you so sensitive to blood?

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: None of your ******* business!
That line again. I knew you'd say that.

She reaches for your bleeding hand, but you erupt into a frenzy of wild flailing. The coppery scent of blood fills the confined space with each frantic movement—and, incredibly, the absurd display actually holds her at bay.
The smell of blood may spread quickly, but your strength is fading faster. Your lungs begin to burn, each breath a ragged gasp.
...No medicine, huh. How did you treat those wounds on your body, then?

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: Those worthless sea beasts? Couldn't kill me if they tried. It's barely an itch. Everything scabs over in a week.
You don't treat the scars on your face either? Not worried about infection?

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: Heh... You think you're still in the city, pretty boy? No one here cares what your face looks like.
steps.female_content: Heh... You think you're still in the city, pretty girl? No one here cares what your face looks like.

steps.content: She grits her teeth and lunges. Instinct takes over; you jerk your bleeding arm high like a shield.
Without food and water, how have you survived?

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: ...I wish I knew.
It's only now you see it: the sunken abdomen, the sharp ribs protruding with each breath—the unmistakable anatomy of prolonged starvation.
But there's food on this island.
My blood for fluids. Flesh for protein. Fresh, and warm. But you didn't take it.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: You're ******* nuts... Is it the hunger talking?
Though her bloodlust seems to have waned, she advances again. This time, evasion is impossible. Your vision tunnels into darkness, and suddenly, your foot slips—
Half your body dangles over the staircase's precipice.
But the fall never comes; a firm grip on your collar hauls you back from the edge.
See? The thought never even occurred to you. Like I said, we're not enemies.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: ...We're not friends, either.
She shoves you against the wall.
Yet you remain unnervingly composed, steadying yourself as if nothing happened and calmly beginning to rebandage your wound.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: You're crazy.
I'll take "crazy" as a compliment. If this place is as bad as you say, a little madness might be the only thing that keeps you sane.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: ...And naive.

She seems thoroughly weary of your amateurish struggle as well, her fighting stance dissolving. Her lean frame slumps heavily against the rusty railing as she tilts her head back to stare at the endlessly coiling stairs above.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: Fine. I'll play along with your little DisCity story. I don't care what you are really up to. But remember one thing—

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: Only the keepers are allowed near the beacon room. Try to go up there, and I'll throw you back into the sea myself.
Before ascending, she casts a final, wary glance over you from head to toe. Then she turns her back and walks away, as if fleeing a plague.
Wait.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: Tsk...
My name is ${PlayerName}. What's yours?
Though visibly irritated, she still stops in her tracks.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: ...Ceto.
[Beach, Daytime]
Ceto forbade you from entering the lantern room at the top of the lighthouse, but she never said anything about exploring elsewhere. And you have—you've scoured nearly every inch of the island.

She wasn't lying. The only medkit you found holds nothing but old bandages, worn so thin they've turned translucent. For water, you've resorted to the most primitive method: manual distillation and condensation. But the Black Tide's complex composition makes purification difficult. Obtaining even a single cup of clear liquid each day feels nothing short of miraculous.
Ceto, who slept curled on the lighthouse windowsill, took a moment to offer what she called advice.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: There are "ingredients" on the north shore. They're all yours.
You never really believed she could be that generous. Now, standing before her so-called ingredients, you stare in disbelief at a mound of corpses—Tide Crawlers—piled high along the shore.
...I'll just stay hungry for now.
You pick up a slimy, limp limb, grimacing as you prepare to fling it back. Then, your motion freezes mid-air. Something about the remains has caught your attention.

More precisely, it's the cutting patterns. These aren't clean blade wounds. They look as though they were made by an irregular, flowing substance that penetrated the flesh, then tore it apart from within. The edges are chaotic, shredded, littered with secondary scratches from embedded debris.
And you're certain that you've seen marks like these before.
[Flashback]

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: The Rancors aren't really weapons; they're more like shapeshifting metal, condensed from the spiritual residue of battlefields. To control one, you need either immense willpower or the external power of Hypercubes.
What happens if someone can't control them?

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: An unstable Rancor will turn on its wielder. It will consume them.
Just like what happened to Jasmine.
[Staircase]
Leaden gray light filters through the dust-caked lattice, slicing Ceto's silhouette into jagged fragments of light and shadow. Sleep is impossible.
She tries to ignore the stranger's scent still clinging to the air, but her bloodshot eyes remain fixed on the knife in her hand—on the constant, faint tremor she cannot steady.

steps.speaker: Voice in Mind
steps.content: Blood... kill him.
